briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Weed Keeps Moving, Psychedelics Keep Winning
briefs.top: Michigan operators are grinding through the 24% wholesale tax with steady demand, fresh store openings, and a growing political coalition for repeal — while nationally, psilocybin's path to FDA approval keeps strengthening even as the DEA rescheduling hearing hits a procedural speed bump. Bottom line: the fundamentals (sales, product pipeline, investor interest) are still pointing up on both fronts.

local.text: Lume opens new Ann Arbor storefront — Michigan-based Lume Cannabis Co. launched its Ann Arbor location at 2247 W. Liberty Street with a grand-opening weekend, adding fresh retail footprint in the Tree Town market.

Wholesale tax collections running far below forecast — the 24% wholesale tax generated only about $37 million in Q2 2026 and $34 million in Q1, against a projected $105 million per quarter, giving repeal advocates fresh ammunition.

Flower prices stay near record lows, demand holds steady — Michigan licensees are largely absorbing the new 24% wholesale tax themselves rather than passing it to shoppers, keeping the state's famously cheap prices intact for now.

Second industry lawsuit keeps tax fight alive — MiCIA's new suit argues the stacked 24% wholesale levy functions as an unconstitutional sales tax on top of the existing 10% excise and 6% sales tax, keeping legal pressure on Lansing.

Governor's race opens a repeal lane for operators — Democratic candidate Chris Swanson publicly pledged to repeal the cannabis wholesale tax while still funding roads, signaling the tax fight is now a live 2026 campaign issue ahead of the Benson-James general.

national.text: Compass Pathways psilocybin nears the finish line — after two positive Phase 3 trials, CEO Kabir Nath says the company is preparing an NDA submission in Q4 2026 and is "closer than ever" to an entirely new mental-health treatment.

FDA fast-tracks three psychedelic therapies — Compass Pathways, Usona Institute, and Transcend Therapeutics all received National Priority Vouchers in April, putting psilocybin and an MDMA-like compound on an accelerated 1-2 month review track with a decision possible by late 2026.

Compass builds out leadership for 2027 launch — the company appointed a new Chief People Officer specifically to help guide the planned commercial rollout of COMP360 psilocybin, targeted for first-half 2027 pending approval.

DEA rescheduling hits a pause, not a dead end — Chief Judge Derek Julius stayed the marijuana rescheduling hearing to weigh a new GAO report, but the stay doesn't touch April's order already placing FDA-approved and state-licensed medical cannabis in Schedule III, and responses are due Oct. 13.

Tilray posts record quarter despite rescheduling jitters — shares hit a 52-week low on the DEA pause, but Tilray's most recent quarter notched record revenue and profit on international sales and BrewDog growth, with another revenue increase expected next week.
